chinelos.note: describes the brinco step: two shuffling steps, then a little jump led with the shoulder, to the band's repetitive beat

pungmul.note: jangdan meters used in pungmul: gutgeori 12 beats, semachi 9/8, hwimori 4/4 or 12/8, jajinmori fast 12/8

circassian-dance.note: instruments of Circassian dance music (pshine accordion, pkhachich clappers, bereban drum, pkhetaw) and meters of named dances (Qaashuo, Zefauk, Sheshen in 4/4)

hand-jive.note: the hand jive sequence step by step: pat thighs twice, cross palms over and under, fists pounded twice each, elbow touches, hitch-hike twice each side

vallenato.note: the four airs: paseo in 4/4 with a strong first beat, son in 4/4 and slowest, merengue and puya in 6/8, puya the fastest; the debate on whether vallenato is danced

zapin.note: Zapin Arab: gambus and marwas, opening sequence, step variations, closing wainab, fast footwork, pairs or groups
Zapin Lenga: six numbered steps with the kopak transition, closing wainab, opening taqsim on the gambus, marwas in pairs setting the tempo, full instrument list
